retention.stated: the disk persists while the plan is paid; the page states no deletion clock

egress.terms: 'Unlimited bandwidth' stated for this plan in the page's own comparison table; the checkout prints no byte quota and no overage price

interface_detail: RDP with administrator access on the issued address; the checkout selects a Windows template and prints its price beside it, which no other row in this set does
tooling: any RDP client; Virtarix client area for rebuild and billing
chaining: the cheapest row in the sweep where the Windows licence is a printed, priced component rather than a sentence, so it is the row to compare against a bring-your-own-licence machine plus a USD 14.17-a-month licence channel.
limits_note: the checkout prints four cycles and no quota: 1 month at USD 27.40 renewing 27.40 on 01/12/2026, 3 months at 27.40 renewing 82.20, 6 months at 27.40 renewing 164.40, and 12 months at 24.66 with a 10 per cent saving renewing 295.92. The first-payment totals it prints are pro-rata figures: USD 32.70 on the monthly cycle and USD 275.65 on the 12-month cycle, neither of which reproduces exactly from the list rate.
binding_note: no byte quota, request rate, object cap or retention clamp is printed anywhere on the offer or the checkout, so nothing in the seven-kind vocabulary binds. The number that decides the row is a price decomposition, not a constraint: 27.40 is 11.40 of machine plus 16.00 of licence.

identity_cost.detail: an account and a payment method at checkout; the rendered checkout prints a total including VAT of USD 32.70, so payment is required before the server exists

reliability_note: no reliability event observed the vendor's own pages disagree on the price by USD 0.20, with the comparison bar printing 27.60 for the same 6 vCPU, 16 GB, 100 GB row that the offer JSON-LD and the checkout price at 27.40.
confidence_note: the plan, the four cycles, the renewal dates, the first-payment totals and the USD 16.00 operating-system line are read from the rendered checkout on 2026-10-26, and the USD 27.40 is corroborated by the page's own offer JSON-LD. The decomposition into a USD 11.40 Linux twin plus a USD 16.00 licence is arithmetic on two printed vendor prices, not a printed sentence, and the two first-payment totals are pro-rata figures that reproduce to within about USD 0.20 rather than exactly. A rendered invoice would settle the pro-rata arithmetic and the 27.40 against 27.60 disagreement; neither touches the licence decomposition, which closes exactly.

quoted: '1 month $27.40', 'Pro Rata until 01/12/2026 $32.70', 'Setup Fee Free', 'Total (incl. VAT) $32.70'; cycles 3 months 82.20, 6 months 164.40, 12 months 24.66 per month renewing 295.92

Plan M on the Linux page is 6 CPU cores, 16 GB RAM and 100 GB NVMe at '$9.12/month first 3 months with 20% discount, then $11.40/month', so 11.40 + 16.00 = 27.40 and the Windows layer is a printed licence line rather than an absorbed cost
the page's comparison bar prints 'Virtarix $27.60 6 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, 100 GB NVMe, Unlimited bandwidth' for the row the checkout bills at 27.40, a self-contradiction on one page

notes: The licence is not an addition to the 27.40; it is a component inside it, and the checkout proves that by pricing the same plan at 11.40 on the Linux page. That makes this row the reference for what a Windows layer costs at a reseller, which is USD 16.00 a month, and it sits beside Kimsufi's separately invoiced USD 34.00 for a 4-core Standard licence. The caveat is arithmetic in the buyer's favour only if they wanted the licence: a buyer with their own key pays 27.40 for a machine whose Linux twin is 11.40.
